questions.solution_text:
On $0\le x\le 3$ the line lies below the $x$-axis.
$-\int_{0}^{3}\left(3x-12\right)dx$
$= -\left[\dfrac{3x^{2}}{2}-12x\right]_{0}^{3}$
$= -\left(\dfrac{27}{2}-36\right)$
$= \dfrac{45}{2}\ \text{units}^{2}$

questions.solution_text:
The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $x=1$.
Let $F(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}-x$, so $F(0)=0$, $F(1)=-\dfrac{2}{3}$ and $F(2)=\dfrac{2}{3}$.
$\int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,dx = -\dfrac{2}{3}$
$\int_{1}^{2} f(x)\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$
$\text{Area} = \dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{4}{3}$
$= 2\ \text{units}^{2}$

questions.solution_text:
On $2\le x\le 3$ the curve lies below the $x$-axis.
$-\int_{2}^{3}\left(-x^{3}\right)dx$
$= -\left[-\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}\right]_{2}^{3}$
$= -\left(-\dfrac{81}{4}+4\right)$
$= \dfrac{65}{4}\ \text{units}^{2}$
